# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

Let me read the input files first per the mandatory reading order. I'll skip the rest of AGENTS.md for now (it's long) — but I should read relevant sections later if needed. Let me read the input files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1223
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1223
- **Title**: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1219` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +74
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:44:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T09:02:07Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. Full `dart test`: the only failures are pre-existing environment issues, verified byte-identical at the base commit — browser-ext e2e needs Chrome (dedicated CI workflow per `dart_test.yaml`), the PTY process-spawn integration tests and the `chatgpt_oauth` socket-bind test fail/skip under this sandbox's concurrency limits, and the trailing `tcache` abort (EXIT=134) is the documented PTY-native teardown race (`test/integration/zz_probe_test.dart`, 2026-10-03).

### Notes

- Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.
- No code-path changes — summary shape, sanitization, and projection are untouched; prompts only. Users with `prompts:` overrides of these files keep their overrides (this changes only the built-ins).

blocks.text:
# gh-1219: compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them

## Description

## Live case (2026-10-04, coordinator session)

During a long multi-agent watch session, a checkpoint/compact (104k → 2.8k) preserved this line:

> "dart #340 validated, awaiting owner approval (pr_approved) — first GOAL-class PR, machine review **may not** auto-approve"

...but cut everything that made the 'may not' checkable (the rule semantics: machine PRs get pr_approved automatically from the review verdict; no human gate exists in the design). Downstream, the agent repeated the surviving assertion as fact ('за тобой 4 аппрува, human gate') for hours across handovers, until the owner challenged it and a 20-minute rule-source dig proved the claim wrong — the approval lane was starving from unrelated rule gaps.

Same pattern with the dev-lane outage: compact kept merge-queue state, dropped dev-lane context → the watch never noticed 5 issues producing 0 PRs for 8h.

## The failure mode

Compaction is truth-neutral: it optimizes for token survival, not epistemic survival.
- A GUESS survives compact indistinguishable from a VERIFIED FACT (the 'may not' hedge was cut with its qualifier).
- CONCLUSIONS survive while their EVIDENCE dies — later, the conclusion can't be re-derived or falsified, only repeated.
- Inherited framing ('owner-approval-gated' in digests) gets laundered into design truth by repetition across compacts/handovers.

In agent-coordination use (multi-day watches, sentinel handovers) this is a correctness bug: the compacted agent confidently asserts wrong state.

## Fix directions

1. **Provenance tags in compact output**: keep [verified] / [assumed] / [hearsay: source] markers on factual claims when summarizing; never strip uncertainty qualifiers ('may', 'suspect', 'unconfirmed').
2. **Evidence-preservation rule**: when compact keeps a conclusion, keep one line of its why (or a pointer to where to re-verify) — conclusions without re-derivation paths are marked for re-verification.
3. **Compact-time re-verification hooks**: claims tagged unverifiable after compact (evidence dropped) could be surfaced to the agent as 're-verify before acting' queue on resume.
4. For handover digests specifically: separate OBSERVED state from INTERPRETED state — sentinels/handovers should never let interpretation masquerade as observation across a compact boundary.

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate]
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || fail "changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || fail "supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || fail "dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          # The remaining legs are path-gated (flutter-analyze covers the
          # lib/bin/test surface; the build-* legs cover platform targets):
          # success or skipped is fine, anything else fails. Branch
          # protection relies on THIS aggregate as the single required
          # check (AGENTS.md "one aggregate Quality gate"), so every needs
          # leg must land here — a red platform build must never yield a
          # green required check.
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
              fail "a leg is $r ($name)"
            fi
          done
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:
    # dart test --tags io
  perf:
    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open
    # budgets. Selected by --tags integration in CI; run standalone with
    # dart test --tags perf
  reg-parity:
    # omp REG parity suite (issue #810): structural diff of the committed
    # omp reference twins vs fa's pure-Dart engine renders. Fast, hermetic
    # (no PTY, no network), SKIPs when the fixtures are not captured yet.

    # aggregate into Quality gate; the pre-commit hook's test-core stage
    # runs the same suite, so hook/CI marker parity holds with no new

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

Let me read the input files first per the mandatory reading order. I'll skip the rest of AGENTS.md for now (it's long) — but I should read relevant sections later if needed. Let me read the input files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1223
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1223
- **Title**: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1219` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +74
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:44:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T09:02:07Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. Full `dart test`: the only failures are pre-existing environment issues, verified byte-identical at the base commit — browser-ext e2e needs Chrome (dedicated CI workflow per `dart_test.yaml`), the PTY process-spawn integration tests and the `chatgpt_oauth` socket-bind test fail/skip under this sandbox's concurrency limits, and the trailing `tcache` abort (EXIT=134) is the documented PTY-native teardown race (`test/integration/zz_probe_test.dart`, 2026-10-03).

### Notes

- Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.
- No code-path changes — summary shape, sanitization, and projection are untouched; prompts only. Users with `prompts:` overrides of these files keep their overrides (this changes only the built-ins).

# gh-1219: compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them

## Description

## Live case (2026-10-04, coordinator session)

During a long multi-agent watch session, a checkpoint/compact (104k → 2.8k) preserved this line:

> "dart #340 validated, awaiting owner approval (pr_approved) — first GOAL-class PR, machine review **may not** auto-approve"

...but cut everything that made the 'may not' checkable (the rule semantics: machine PRs get pr_approved automatically from the review verdict; no human gate exists in the design). Downstream, the agent repeated the surviving assertion as fact ('за тобой 4 аппрува, human gate') for hours across handovers, until the owner challenged it and a 20-minute rule-source dig proved the claim wrong — the approval lane was starving from unrelated rule gaps.

Same pattern with the dev-lane outage: compact kept merge-queue state, dropped dev-lane context → the watch never noticed 5 issues producing 0 PRs for 8h.

## The failure mode

Compaction is truth-neutral: it optimizes for token survival, not epistemic survival.
- A GUESS survives compact indistinguishable from a VERIFIED FACT (the 'may not' hedge was cut with its qualifier).
- CONCLUSIONS survive while their EVIDENCE dies — later, the conclusion can't be re-derived or falsified, only repeated.
- Inherited framing ('owner-approval-gated' in digests) gets laundered into design truth by repetition across compacts/handovers.

In agent-coordination use (multi-day watches, sentinel handovers) this is a correctness bug: the compacted agent confidently asserts wrong state.

## Fix directions

1. **Provenance tags in compact output**: keep [verified] / [assumed] / [hearsay: source] markers on factual claims when summarizing; never strip uncertainty qualifiers ('may', 'suspect', 'unconfirmed').
2. **Evidence-preservation rule**: when compact keeps a conclusion, keep one line of its why (or a pointer to where to re-verify) — conclusions without re-derivation paths are marked for re-verification.
3. **Compact-time re-verification hooks**: claims tagged unverifiable after compact (evidence dropped) could be surfaced to the agent as 're-verify before acting' queue on resume.
4. For handover digests specifically: separate OBSERVED state from INTERPRETED state — sentinels/handovers should never let interpretation masquerade as observation across a compact boundary.

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate]
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.
          [ "$R_CHANGES" = "success" ] || fail "changes classifier = $R_CHANGES"
          # Security legs must EXECUTE and pass. For these, skipped is a
          # dodge (e.g. a cunning diff that makes the classifier misfire),
          # not a pass — review follow-up, #796/#801.
          [ "$R_SUPPLY_CHAIN" = "success" ] || fail "supply-chain = $R_SUPPLY_CHAIN (skipped security is a dodge)"
          [ "$R_DEP_AUDIT" = "success" ] || fail "dep-audit = $R_DEP_AUDIT (skipped security is a dodge)"
          # The remaining legs are path-gated (flutter-analyze covers the
          # lib/bin/test surface; the build-* legs cover platform targets):
          # success or skipped is fine, anything else fails. Branch
          # protection relies on THIS aggregate as the single required
          # check (AGENTS.md "one aggregate Quality gate"), so every needs
          # leg must land here — a red platform build must never yield a
          # green required check.
          for kv in "static:$R_STATIC" "flutter-analyze:$R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE" "test-core:$R_TEST_CORE" "coverage-gate:$R_COVERAGE" \
                    "guards:$R_GUARDS" "flutter-tests:$R_FLUTTER" "app-crap-gate:$R_CRAP" \
                    "test-faui:$R_FAUI" "perf-gate:$R_PERF" "cube-kernel-live:$R_CUBE" \
                    "cli-visual-settings:$R_CLI_VISUAL" "build-web:$R_BUILD_WEB" \
                    "build-android:$R_BUILD_ANDROID" "build-ios:$R_BUILD_IOS" "build-macos:$R_BUILD_MACOS" \
                    "integration-mock:$R_INTEG" "hostile-env:$R_HOSTILE" \
                    "pty-integration-linux:$R_PTY_LINUX" "pty-coverage-gate:$R_PTY_GATES" "pty-visual:$R_PTY_VISUAL" \
                    "installer-verify:$R_INSTALLER_VERIFY" "install-pin-gate:$R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE"; do
            name="${kv%%:*}"; r="${kv#*:}"
            if [ "$r" != "success" ] && [ "$r" != "skipped" ]; then
              fail "a leg is $r ($name)"
            fi
          done
          echo "Quality gate OK"

  # Issue #303 (the #262 DoD): the perf-tagged e2e gate must red-block the
  # MERGE, not only the release — before #551 the only integration leg
  # outside PRs was tag-time, and perf stays excluded from integration-mock.
  # This leg runs the same

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:

    if: >-

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger …

Let me read the input files first per the mandatory reading order. I'll skip the rest of AGENTS.md for now (it's long) — but I should read relevant sections later if needed. Let me read the input files.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1223
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1223
- **Title**: gh-1219 compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1219` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +74
- **Deletions**: -7
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T07:44:23Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T09:02:07Z

## PR Description

### Root Cause

Compaction checkpoints were truth-neutral: the summarizer prompts said "Preserve EVERY fact" but had no rule keeping an uncertainty qualifier attached to its claim, no provenance tagging, and no evidence requirement for kept conclusions. A hedge like "machine review **may not** auto-approve" and its rule context competed for tokens on equal footing with hard facts, so a compacted agent could inherit the conclusion, lose the qualifier and evidence, and repeat the assumption as fact across every later turn. The loss happens entirely at summarization time — `summary_sanitizer.dart` never strips hedges — so the fix is the prompt contract itself.

### Fix

- `prompts/compaction/summary_system.md`: added the canonical epistemic-status rule — uncertainty qualifiers ("may", "suspect", "unconfirmed") stay verbatim with their claims (never detach/upgrade); claims are tagged `[verified]` / `[assumed]` / `[hearsay: source]` by how they are known; every kept conclusion carries one line of its why or the marker `unverified — re-verify` (the ticket's direction-3 re-verify queue, delivered inline in the checkpoint re-read every turn). The system prompt rides every summarization call: classic first summary, update fold, turn prefix, and the structured engine's checkpoint pass.
- `prompts/compaction/branch_summary.md`: handover digests now separate `## Observed State` (witnessed, with what produced it) from `## Interpreted State` (each inference names its observation; no observation = `unverified — re-verify`) — direction 4; unevidenced claims are never laundered into Observed State.
- `prompts/compaction/structured_checkpoint.md`, `turn_prefix.md`: same hedge/evidence rules on the instruction tails.
- `prompts/compaction/summary_update.md`: one budget-fitting rule — "PRESERVE provenance tags and hedges verbatim — never upgrade a hedge".
- `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart`: regenerated.

Constraint honored: issue #81 AC7 pins the net instruction delta of `summary.md` + `summary_update.md` at ≤500 chars, with only 77 chars of headroom left — the full contract therefore lives in the system prompt, not the budgeted task-prompt bodies.

### Test Coverage

- `test/compaction/compaction_test.dart`: 5 new pins — the epistemic contract on the system prompt (hedges, `[verified]`/`[assumed]`/`[hearsay]`, `unverified — re-verify`), the update-fold never-upgrade rule, turn-prefix hedges, structured-checkpoint evidence rule, and Observed/Interpreted separation in branch summaries. All failed before the prompt change (RED), pass after.
- `test/compaction/summary_sanitizer_test.dart`: hedge-survival pin — the pipeline's only mechanical strip point never rewrites "may not auto-approve", `[assumed]`, or "unconfirmed".
- AC7 budget test (`net instruction delta`): 494 ≤ 500 on the committed state.
- All 291 compaction/prompts tests pass. Full `dart test`: the only failures are pre-existing environment issues, verified byte-identical at the base commit — browser-ext e2e needs Chrome (dedicated CI workflow per `dart_test.yaml`), the PTY process-spawn integration tests and the `chatgpt_oauth` socket-bind test fail/skip under this sandbox's concurrency limits, and the trailing `tcache` abort (EXIT=134) is the documented PTY-native teardown race (`test/integration/zz_probe_test.dart`, 2026-10-03).

### Notes

- Direction 3's standalone "re-verify queue on resume" surface is covered minimally: the `unverified — re-verify` marker lands in the checkpoint text the agent re-reads every turn; a dedicated mechanical queue (session records driving a resume notice) is a larger feature, intentionally out of scope for this fix.
- No code-path changes — summary shape, sanitization, and projection are untouched; prompts only. Users with `prompts:` overrides of these files keep their overrides (this changes only the built-ins).

blocks.text:
# gh-1219: compact: preserve epistemic status of claims — compaction keeps assertions but drops the evidence/uncertainty that would falsify them

## Description

## Live case (2026-10-04, coordinator session)

During a long multi-agent watch session, a checkpoint/compact (104k → 2.8k) preserved this line:

> "dart #340 validated, awaiting owner approval (pr_approved) — first GOAL-class PR, machine review **may not** auto-approve"

...but cut everything that made the 'may not' checkable (the rule semantics: machine PRs get pr_approved automatically from the review verdict; no human gate exists in the design). Downstream, the agent repeated the surviving assertion as fact ('за тобой 4 аппрува, human gate') for hours across handovers, until the owner challenged it and a 20-minute rule-source dig proved the claim wrong — the approval lane was starving from unrelated rule gaps.

Same pattern with the dev-lane outage: compact kept merge-queue state, dropped dev-lane context → the watch never noticed 5 issues producing 0 PRs for 8h.

## The failure mode

Compaction is truth-neutral: it optimizes for token survival, not epistemic survival.
- A GUESS survives compact indistinguishable from a VERIFIED FACT (the 'may not' hedge was cut with its qualifier).
- CONCLUSIONS survive while their EVIDENCE dies — later, the conclusion can't be re-derived or falsified, only repeated.
- Inherited framing ('owner-approval-gated' in digests) gets laundered into design truth by repetition across compacts/handovers.

In agent-coordination use (multi-day watches, sentinel handovers) this is a correctness bug: the compacted agent confidently asserts wrong state.

## Fix directions

1. **Provenance tags in compact output**: keep [verified] / [assumed] / [hearsay: source] markers on factual claims when summarizing; never strip uncertainty qualifiers ('may', 'suspect', 'unconfirmed').
2. **Evidence-preservation rule**: when compact keeps a conclusion, keep one line of its why (or a pointer to where to re-verify) — conclusions without re-derivation paths are marked for re-verification.
3. **Compact-time re-verification hooks**: claims tagged unverifiable after compact (evidence dropped) could be surfaced to the agent as 're-verify before acting' queue on resume.
4. For handover digests specifically: separate OBSERVED state from INTERPRETED state — sentinels/handovers should never let interpretation masquerade as observation across a compact boundary.

quality-gate:
    name: Quality gate
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [changes, static, flutter-analyze, test-core, coverage-gate, guards, flutter-tests, app-crap-gate, test-faui, perf-gate, cli-visual-settings, cube-kernel-live, build-web, build-android, build-ios, build-macos, integration-mock, hostile-env, pty-integration-linux, pty-coverage-gate, pty-visual, supply-chain, dep-audit, installer-verify, install-pin-gate]
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - name: Report leg results
        run: |
          echo "static        = ${{ needs.static.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "test-core     = ${{ needs.test-core.result }}"
          echo "coverage-gate = ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "guards        = ${{ needs.guards.result }}"
          echo "flutter-analyze = ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}"
          echo "flutter-tests = ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}"
          echo "test-faui     = ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}"
          echo "app-crap-gate = ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}"
          echo "perf-gate     = ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}"
          echo "cube-live     = ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}"
          echo "cli-visual    = ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}"
          echo "build-web     = ${{ needs.build-web.result }}"
          echo "build-android = ${{ needs.build-android.result }}"
          echo "build-ios     = ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}"
          echo "build-macos   = ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}"
          echo "integ-mock    = ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}"
          echo "hostile-env   = ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}"
          echo "pty-integ-linux = ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}"
          echo "pty-gates     = ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}"
          echo "pty-visual    = ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}"
          echo "supply-chain  = ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}"
          echo "dep-audit     = ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}"
          echo "installer-it = ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}"
          echo "pin-gate    = ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}"
      - name: Fail on any real failure (skipped security = dodge = FAIL)
        env:
          R_CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          R_SUPPLY_CHAIN: ${{ needs.supply-chain.result }}
          R_DEP_AUDIT: ${{ needs.dep-audit.result }}
          R_STATIC: ${{ needs.static.result }}
          R_FLUTTER_ANALYZE: ${{ needs.flutter-analyze.result }}
          R_TEST_CORE: ${{ needs.test-core.result }}
          R_COVERAGE: ${{ needs.coverage-gate.result }}
          R_GUARDS: ${{ needs.guards.result }}
          R_FLUTTER: ${{ needs.flutter-tests.result }}
          R_CRAP: ${{ needs.app-crap-gate.result }}
          R_FAUI: ${{ needs.test-faui.result }}
          R_PERF: ${{ needs.perf-gate.result }}
          R_CUBE: ${{ needs.cube-kernel-live.result }}
          R_CLI_VISUAL: ${{ needs.cli-visual-settings.result }}
          R_BUILD_WEB: ${{ needs.build-web.result }}
          R_BUILD_ANDROID: ${{ needs.build-android.result }}
          R_BUILD_IOS: ${{ needs.build-ios.result }}
          R_BUILD_MACOS: ${{ needs.build-macos.result }}
          R_INTEG: ${{ needs.integration-mock.result }}
          R_HOSTILE: ${{ needs.hostile-env.result }}
          R_PTY_LINUX: ${{ needs.pty-integration-linux.result }}
          R_PTY_GATES: ${{ needs.pty-coverage-gate.result }}
          R_PTY_VISUAL: ${{ needs.pty-visual.result }}
          R_INSTALLER_VERIFY: ${{ needs.installer-verify.result }}
          R_INSTALL_PIN_GATE: ${{ needs.install-pin-gate.result }}
        run: |
          fail() { echo "Quality gate FAILED: $1"; exit 1; }
          # The classifier itself must have run: a failed or skipped
          # classifier skips EVERY downstream leg and would wave a PR
          # through with zero gates executed.

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@e611e5f4240e9c8a5cdbf10721562eb04513d006
    with:
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

- uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ~/.pub-cache
          key: pub-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}

      - run: dart pub get

      - name: File size guard (no dart file over 2800 lines)
        run: |
          violations=$(find lib test example -name '*.dart' \
            ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' ! -name '*.mocks.dart' \
            -exec sh -c 'lines=$(wc -l < "$1"); if [ "$lines" -gt 2800 ]; then echo "$1: $lines lines"; fi' _ {} \;)
          if [ -n "$violations" ]; then echo "$violations"; exit 1; fi

      # Issue #1100: the fa-web-spa.zip packaging guard (base-tag patch +
      # absolute-/app/ grep) must stay functional on every PR — a release
      # run is the wrong place to first discover a broken guard. Fixture
      # self-test: positive path + all red exits, pure bash, no web build.
      - name: Web SPA packaging guard self-test (#1100)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          d=$(mktemp -d)
          trap 'rm -rf "$d"' EXIT
          mkdir -p "$d/build"
          printf '<html><head>\n<base href="/app/">\n</head></html>\n' > "$d/build/index.html"
          for f in flutter_service_worker.js flutter_bootstrap.js; do echo "// $f" > "$d/build/$f"; done
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/out.zip" > /dev/null
          unzip -p "$d/out.zip" index.html | grep -F '<base href="./">'
          # AC4 pin: packaging never mutates its input — the Pages deploy's
          # build dir must stay byte-identical.
          grep -F '<base href="/app/">' "$d/build/index.html"
          # Red exit 1: an absolute /app/ sneaking into a touchpoint.
          echo '{"x":"/app/y"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed a build containing /app/ (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 2: no base tag to patch.
          echo '{"name":"fa"}' > "$d/build/manifest.json"
          echo '<html></html>' > "$d/build/index.html"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad2.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an unpatchable base tag (AC1 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Red exit 3: a missing touchpoint file.
          rm "$d/build/manifest.json"
          if bash scripts/package_web_spa.sh "$d/build" "$d/bad3.zip" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "::error::package_web_spa guard passed an incomplete build (AC3 #1100)"
            exit 1
          fi
          # fa1.dev parity pin: both web builds must keep the identical
          # release flags AND the same pinned SDK — the bundle's only edit
          # stays the base tag.
          for wf in .github/workflows/pages.yml .github/workflows/ci.yml; do
            grep -q -- '--release' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost the --release web flag (#1100 parity)"; exit 1; }
            grep -q -- '--base-href /app/' "$wf" || { echo "::error::$wf lost --base-href /app/ (#1100 parity, pages + bundle must share it)"; exit 1; }

tags:
  integration:
    # Integration tests spawn real processes / network and are excluded from the
    # pre-commit gate. Run them manually with: dart test --tags integration
  browser-ext:
    # Headless-Chrome extension suite (test/browser_ext/). CI runs it only
    # through the dedicated browser-ext.yml workflow (builds sw/agent.js and
    # supplies Chrome for Testing); ci.yml's tag job excludes it:
    # dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext
  llm:
    # Real-provider smoke tests (issue #551): hit live provider APIs and need
    # secrets. They carry `integration` too and run ONLY in the tag-only
    # provider-smoke job (v* tags) and nightly — every per-PR suite excludes
    # them: dart test --exclude-tags llm
    #
    # Rate limiting (issue #931 part 3.3): package:test forbids `concurrency`
    # in tag overrides (test_core _disallow('concurrency') for tag scopes, v1.32),
    # so the pin lives on the CI invocations: the per-PR integration shards run
    # `--concurrency=4`, which bounds concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB at
    # 4 (they previously ran at the default = CPU count). gh-1005 (2026-09-30)
    # retired the mac leg: the per-PR suite runs ONCE (pty-integration-linux,
    # 3 shards x 4 = 12 concurrent live tests) and nightly's unsharded leg
    # runs hours later — the old mac+linux same-window doubling (24) is gone.
    # If provider 429s start flaking the leg, lower the knob; per-job rate
    # pinning across CI jobs has no native Actions primitive.
  pty:
    # Child-agent-spawn PTY tests (issue #553): the test drives a full task
    # tool spawn — a second CLI process whose boot/JIT time is unbounded on a
    # loaded runner. They carry `integration` too and run in the per-PR
    # sharded legs (the shard manifest includes them — bounded
    # --concurrency, prewarmed boots) and nightly; the no-key
    # integration-mock leg still excludes them: dart test --exclude-tags pty
  io:
    # IO tests use dart:io primitives (local sockets, processes) and are
    # excluded from the default pre-commit gate. Run them with:

    # Perf gates (issue #262): generate large fixtures and assert open

project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK
